For the stopping diagnostics, write $F_D=J_D$ and $F_A=-J_A$, with the opponent's plan fixed. Let $\widetilde z_p$ be the numerical unilateral response and let $\mathcal C_D=U_K$ and $\mathcal C_A=A_K$. The discovered improvement is $gap_p=\max\{0,F_p(z_p)-F_p(\widetilde z_p)\}$. We use the unit-step projected-gradient residual $stat_p=\|z_p-\Pi_{\mathcal C_p}(z_p-\nabla F_p(z_p))\|_\infty$ and the response distance $dist_p=\|\widetilde z_p-z_p\|_\infty$, where $\Pi$ is Euclidean projection onto the bounded, capacity-constrained feasible set. Response candidates are accepted only if their bound and capacity violations are at most $10^{-10}$. The single-start checks used for stopping are distinct from the three-start searches performed after termination.

The archived optimization used Python 3.11.7, NumPy 1.26.4, and SciPy 1.11.4 on Windows. The base random seeds were 20262114, 20261114, and 20263114 for capacities 0.6, 1.2, and 1.8, respectively; the random full-run initialization used the corresponding base seed plus two. The uniform-start plan was selected for reporting. Saved controls, trajectories, diagnostic records, and figure-generation inputs accompany the manuscript source.

All three uniform-start paths first met the stopping criteria after five alternating updates. Across the three capacities and both players, the normalized discovered improvement, current-plan projected residual, and response distance did not exceed $2.90\times10^{-10}$, $6.48\times10^{-5}$, and $3.35\times10^{-5}$, respectively; all final single-start SLSQP exit codes were zero. The largest control difference between full-run initializations was below $4.02\times10^{-5}$. Separate three-start checks of the final reported plans also passed the stated local criteria. For the three main-capacity comparison plans, increasing RK4 substeps per control interval from 48 to 192 changed shared-time states by at most $8.71\times10^{-12}$. These are numerical diagnostics within the specified strategy class.
